results.title: Printed Circuit Boards in United States Trade
results.content:
In June 2026, United States exported Printed Circuit Boards mostly to Mexico ($28.4M), Malaysia ($7.94M), Germany ($7.8M), Canada ($7.29M), and China ($4.04M). During the same month, United States imported Printed Circuit Boards mostly from China ($81.4M), Chinese Taipei ($67.4M), Thailand ($23.9M), Vietnam ($21.3M), and South Korea ($15.5M).

#### Growth [...] ## Latest Trends

### June 2026

#### Overview

In June 2026, United States exported $90.4M and imported $281M of Printed Circuit Boards, resulting in a negative trade balance of $190M. Between May 2026 and June 2026, the exports of Printed Circuit Boards from United States decreased by $55M (-37.8%), from $145M to $90.4M. During the same period, imports increased by $23.7M (9.22%), from $257M to $281M.

#### Origins and Destinations [...] In June 2026, the year-on-year exports of Printed Circuit Boards from United States increased by 9.31%. This was explained primarily by an increase in exports to Germany (+$4.9M or 169%), Mexico (+$4.73M or 20%), and Singapore (+$1.4M or 67.3%). During the same month, year-on-year imports of Printed Circuit Boards to United States increased by 23.7%. This was explained primarily by an increase in imports from China (+$23.1M or 39.5%), Vietnam (+$10.7M or 101%), and Mexico (+$7.74M or 205%).

results.title: Electronics Manufacturing Services for 2026 Tariff Mitigation
results.content:
China, which manufactures more than 50% of the world’s printed circuit boards, has been particularly affected by the tariffs. Plans were finalized for semiconductor tariffs to rise to 50% under the China review. This measure is aimed at chips, but it pulls through costs into many electronic assemblies that sit on PCBs. Additionally, the USTR extended some expiring exclusions into 2026. Many categories lost their exclusions, including some printed circuit board assemblies, which means those [...] Check the country of origin and classification of imported products carefully. Tariffs differ between bare printed circuit boards and PCBAs, so any errors in classification could be costly. Country of origin is important because moving certain assembly steps outside of China can legally change the product’s origin and reduce tariff exposure. [...] ### The Direct Impacts of Tariffs on PCBA Prices

When it comes to tariffs, bare PCBs are classified differently than printed circuit board assemblies. Because of this, they face different tariff rules. If a tariff exemption on PCBAs expires, companies may suddenly have to pay the full tariff rate again. Making sure PCBAs are classified correctly and the country of origin is properly documented can make a big difference in final costs for your company.

The regulatory landscape for electronics imports shifted twice in February 2026, creating a new “stack” of duties on Chinese-origin components and boards.

results.title: How Tariffs Are Affecting the PCB Circuit Board Industry
results.content: China — the largest producer of PCBs in the world — has been the primary target of the administration’s tariffs. As such, imported goods from China currently face the highest country-specific tariff rates of any nation in the world, with the average imported good facing a 30% tariff at the very least. However, even this lowered tariff rate may not last, as it is the result of a 90-day trade agreement between the U.S. and China. [...] As such, each business relying on PCBs will need to evaluate its own supply chain to determine the specific effect of tariffs on its import prices. Even if your business is not importing fully functional PCBs from China or Mexico, you may still have to deal with increased prices on copper, semiconductors and other PCB components. The import price may be lower overall, but it will still be increased by the universal 10% tariff at a bare minimum. [...] At present, there is a 10% universal tariff on most goods imported to the U.S. However, individual nations and specific goods have also been targeted with their own specific tariffs based on the status of their trade relationship. Japanese cars, for instance, face a 25% tariff. At the moment, there are no U.S. tariffs on printed circuit board imports specifically. However, imported PCBs and their components and materials are still subjected to both the universal 10% tariff and the tariffs
